title: Scoped PRD: Hosted Multi-Protocol Endpoint Acceptance Flightplan
creator: Elaine Park
description: This PRD defines a scoped acceptance and launch flightplan for the hosted inference surface that consolidates chat, completion, embedding, and rerank endpoints into a single, multi-protocol offering. The goal is to remove ambiguity in API semantics, set measurable acceptance gates, and provide an operational rollout checklist that minimizes customer disruption. This document focuses on behavioral contracts, telemetry/eval requirements, backward compatibility constraints for client SDKs, and a staged canary rollout strategy with automated rollback triggers.
requirements_clarifications: Protocol compatibility: clear rules for HTTP JSON and streaming websocket/HTTP2 streams; streaming chunks must preserve token order and chunk boundaries across SDKs.
Completions vs Chat semantics: define canonical mapping of chat messages -> internals for temperature/top_p defaults and the expected deterministic fallback behavior when caller pins seeds.
Embedding normalization: embeddings returned should be L2-normalized and documented; include exact pre/post processing expected for cosine similarity consumers.
Rerank contract: accept list-of-candidates + query, return ordered indices with optional per-item scores and a defined tie-breaking algorithm.
Error model: standardized error codes for transient capacity (RATE_LIMITED_CAPACITY), model-fallback, prompt-too-long, and validation errors with suggested client retry/backoff behavior.
Cost telemetry: expose per-request token accounting and a summarized per-route cost estimate for dashboarding; specify tokenization library/version used for accounting.
Backwards compatibility: maintain existing top-level field names for at least two release cycles; any rename must include a deprecation header and automated mapping in SDKs.
Safety/guardrails: document default output filters and a path for customers to opt into more permissive lanes via security-reviewed contracts.
Latency semantics for streaming: first-byte latency SLO and steady-state inter-chunk time expectations (see acceptance criteria).
scope_boundaries: IN: hosted chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints for the public API (multi-tenant).
IN: SDK adapters (Python/Node/Go) for the new streaming semantics and compatibility shims.
IN: Behavioral eval harness and canonical prompt suites for regression detection.
OUT: private/VPC on-prem packaging and Dedicated capacity lifecycle changes (handled in separate initiative).
OUT: multimodal/image/video endpoint expansion (out of scope for this launch).
OUT: Billing model redesign; we will use existing token/unit billing for initial rollout.
OUT: Major model architecture changes (quantization or alternate kernel paths) unless transparently compatible with API surface.
scope_changes: Original target included deterministic seed support across all lanes; scope reduced to deterministic seeding for completions and chat only (rerank/embeddings deferred) to reduce client SDK work.
Initial acceptance for embeddings loosened: cosine correlation baseline set to within ±0.03 of golden set (was ±0.01) to enable earlier rollout while we tune normalization edgecases.
Streaming chunk contract simplified to 'ordered-chunks' without strict chunk-size guarantees to avoid blocking on transport-layer fragmentation fixes.
Removed mandatory per-token cost header from the first launch; will be added in the first maintenance release after instrumentation completes.
acceptance_criteria: API contract verification: all endpoints pass an automated contract test suite (OpenAPI schema + golden request/response samples).
Behavioral regression: daily eval runs on canonical prompt sets show no more than 1% regression in top-level quality metrics (LLM-specific evals defined in telemetry plan).
Latency SLOs: P95 < 350ms and P99 < 900ms for typical short completion requests (<128 tokens) in the us-west region under baseline load test profile.
Streaming latency: first-byte < 150ms P95 for average short-turn chat messages; inter-chunk jitter must be < 60ms median for streaming responses under baseline load.
Throughput: the hosted pool must sustain target QPS of 120 req/s for the chosen instance class with autoscaling rules validated in integration tests.
Compatibility: official SDKs (Python/Node) must provide compatibility shims so existing clients using older field names do not crash; at least two major SDK versions validated.
Operational: deployable canary with 5% traffic slice and automatic rollback if error rate > 2% or latency breach > 5x for 5 consecutive minutes.
Observability: request tracing, per-route token counts, and business-metric dashboards available with 7-day retention for launch; alerting on quality regression, latency, and cost anomalies.
Security & Compliance: security review completed and any required KMS changes documented; data egress flags validated with legal for EU customers.
launch_checklist: Finalize PRD and publish to Confluence with links to SDK migration notes.
Merge API contract PRs and tag release branch; create a release candidate build.
Complete SDK updates (Python/Node/Go) and publish pre-release packages; verify backward compatibility with sample apps.
Run full integration and chaos tests including canary rollback scenarios and failover to fallback model variants.
Provision canary capacity and configure traffic-shaping policies (5% canary -> 25% -> ramp to 100% with health gates).
Enable telemetry pipeline: ensure eval harness, Datadog dashboards, and alerting are live on release candidate.
Ops runbook and postmortem template published; on-call rotation and pager escalation added for the first 72 hours of launch.
Customer comms: prepare launch notes, migration guidance, and expected performance profiles; identify early adopter customers for proactive outreach.
Legal & security signoff: confirm security review required items are closed or have tracked compensating controls.
Cutover: coordinate with infra to perform zero-downtime cutover and monitor for error/latency anomalies during ramp.
Fallthrough: validate automatic model variant fallbacks and documented manual rollback steps in case of non-automated incidents.
monitoring_and_eval_plan: Canonical prompt suites: 3k prompts covering hallucination, safety, contextual continuity, and embedding similarity edgecases to run nightly.
Quality alerts: regression alert if nightly eval score drops by >1% on any critical metric or if embeddings similarity AUC drops by >0.02.
Telemetry events: include fields request_id, route, model_version, token_count, runtime_ms, error_tags, and consumer_tier for each request.
Dashboards: prebuilt dashboards for latency, error-rate, token economics, and model-fallback events with 7-day and 90-day views.
Post-launch audit: 14-day review meeting with Eng/ML/PD to assess early metrics and decide on any immediate mitigations or scope roll-forwards.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: behavioral regressions introduced by model variant changes. Mitigation: gate model swaps behind nightly eval score thresholds and canary slices.
Risk: subtle embedding normalization differences break downstream similarity services. Mitigation: publish exact normalization math and provide a compatibility-mode flag in embeddings API.
Risk: streaming semantics differences across SDKs cause integration bugs. Mitigation: ship explicit integration tests and sample apps that validate chunk ordering and reconnection behavior.
Risk: insufficient observability during ramp. Mitigation: require green telemetry smoke tests before increasing canary traffic and hold capacity until dashboards are verified.
notes: We intentionally scoped down deterministic seeding to speed customer availability; reevaluate for v1.1.
Coordinate with Dedicated and Private teams for eventual parity; this PRD does not alter their SLAs.
Keep prompt suite under source control and invite early-feedback from two anchor customers during the canary window.
